title: Mastering Intraday Market Breadth & Stock Point Contribution
author: TradersDesk Quantitative Research
excerpt: Learn how reading constituent point contribution and advance/decline participation prevents false breakout traps during major index expiries.
content:
# Mastering Intraday Market Breadth & Stock Point Contribution

Many retail traders lose money trading NIFTY index breakouts because they look only at the spot index price. If Reliance and HDFC Bank rally by 1.5%, Nifty can surge 80 points even if 35 out of 50 stocks are falling!

---

## The Divergence Trap

When you see:
1. **Index Spot making New Highs**, but
2. **Breadth % stalling below 40% (O-Dominance)**

This is a classic **Heavyweight Skew Divergence**. Institutional smart money frequently uses 1 or 2 mega-cap stocks to prop up the index while distributing mid and large-cap holdings across the board.

---

## How to Trade With TradersDesk Breadth Desk

- **Rule 1: Confluence Check**
  Never take a trend-following long trade unless Breadth % is above its **20 SMA** and Advancing stocks outnumber Decliners (`X > 25`).
- **Rule 2: Drag vs Support Split Bar**
  Check the **Net Points Badge** at the bottom of the Breadth desk. If the dragging points exceed supporting points, any morning spike is prone to aggressive mean-reversion.

> *"Trade the market that is actually participating, not just the index headline."*

title: Decoding FII Institutional Derivatives Positioning & OI Matrix
author: TradersDesk Quantitative Research
excerpt: How to interpret Client vs FII vs Proprietary option writing and index futures long/short contracts to identify market turning points.
content:
# Decoding FII Institutional Derivatives Positioning & OI Matrix

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) trade with massive capital reserves. Unlike retail participants who mostly buy out-of-the-money (OTM) options, FIIs and Proprietary desks operate as net option writers and futures hedgers.

---

## The 4 Market Participants

1. **Client (Retail & HNIs)**: High volume of Call/Put buyers, typically long gamma.
2. **DII (Domestic Mutual Funds & Insurance)**: Primarily long equity, occasional protective put hedges.
3. **FII (Foreign Portfolio Investors)**: Sophisticated multi-leg arbitrage, index futures directional bias.
4. **Pro (Proprietary Trading Desks / Broker Arbitrageurs)**: Market makers, short volatility sellers.

---

## Reading the Smart Money Matrix

When FII Index Futures Long % drops below **15%**, historical data shows extreme exhaustion in selling, setting up explosive short-covering rallies.
